Consult Summary:
- Adult patient with 2-day history of constant, worsening suprapubic pain, subjective feverishness, urinary frequency, and pink urine; treated empirically for presumed acute uncomplicated cystitis, with pregnancy test advised and safety-net follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal (just below umbilicus) pain; patient feels hot/sweaty.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began ~2 days ago; gradual onset; constant and worsening.
- Character/location: Burning pain, localized below the belly button; tender to pressure; no radiation reported.
- Bowel: Constipation last week (resolved); no current diarrhea; bowel movements now normal.
- Urinary: Increased frequency; urine noted “a little pink”; denies burning/stinging with urination.
- Nausea/vomiting: Mild nausea; no vomiting.
- Fever: Felt hot and sweaty; no measured temperature.
- Gynecologic/sexual: Sexually active with one partner; last intercourse 4 days ago; etonogestrel implant (Implanon) in place ~1 year; still has periods; LMP ~2 weeks ago; last STI screen 6 months ago negative.
- Pertinent negatives (ROS): No shortness of breath, cough, palpitations, headaches, or vision changes.
- Patient preference: Agreed to empiric antibiotics and monitoring; open to pregnancy testing.

Past Medical History:
- Generally well per patient.
- No prior surgeries.
- No prior similar episodes reported.

Medications:
- Current: Implanon (etonogestrel implant) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- New prescription: Trimethoprim — 1 tablet twice daily for 3 days (dose/route not documented).
- Analgesia advised: Paracetamol — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: Not recorded.

Social History:
- Lives in a shared house with two roommates.
- Occupation: Accountant.
- Tobacco: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Social use.
- Sexual history: Monogamous with one partner; no barrier contraception; last intercourse 4 days ago.

Family History:
- No relevant family history reported.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Examination findings: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None performed during this consult.
- Pregnancy test recommended (not yet done).

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Suprapubic pain with urinary frequency and possible hematuria, mild nausea, and subjective feverishness without dysuria — most consistent with acute uncomplicated cystitis. Pregnancy not excluded. Alternatives (e.g., urolithiasis, early appendicitis) considered if symptoms evolve.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Acute uncomplicated cystitis: Supported by suprapubic pain, frequency, pink urine; absence of dysuria does not exclude.
  - Urolithiasis (distal ureter/bladder): Pink urine and lower abdominal pain support; pain is constant burning without colic and no flank pain reported (opposes).
  - Early appendicitis: Gradual worsening pain with mild nausea supports; localization midline/suprapubic and lack of RLQ migration or vomiting oppose.

- Issue 1: Suspected acute uncomplicated cystitis
  - Plan:
    - Start trimethoprim as prescribed (1 tablet twice daily for 3 days).
    - Hydration encouraged; cranberry juice optional as discussed.
    - Analgesia with paracetamol as needed.
    - Safety net: Return/call urgently for worsening abdominal pain, persistent/worsening feverishness, vomiting, or if not improving within a few days.

- Issue 2: Pregnancy not yet excluded
  - Plan:
    - Perform a pregnancy test as advised to rule out pregnancy-related causes.

- Issue 3: Unclear etiology if no improvement (consider stones/appendicitis if evolution of symptoms)
  - Plan:
    - Tests were discussed initially; empiric treatment chosen.
    - Reassess if symptoms persist or worsen to guide further evaluation.

- General plan items:
  - Prescription sent to patient’s pharmacy.
  - Follow-up in a few days if no improvement, sooner if red flags occur.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies not recorded; vitals and physical exam not recorded; no urinalysis/culture documented; pregnancy status pending test.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted regarding clinical impression; both align on suspected cystitis.
- Transcript quality: Patient name referred to as “Tim” and “Kim” at different points (inconsistency); otherwise clear.
